subject: Integration telemetry + graceful fallback plan for Keystone
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Integration telemetry + graceful fallback plan for Keystone

Samir / Priya —

Great to meet yesterday. As promised, I wanted to capture a concise blueprint our Implementation team will follow for SDK instrumentation, retry/backoff behavior, and endpoint cutover so your engineering team can review before we schedule the handoff session. High level:

- SDK setup: install official Redwood client, enable structured telemetry hooks (events + traces).
- Retries/timeouts: linear jittered backoff for idempotent requests; exponential for token-generation flows with max 5 retries.
- Rate-limit handling: surface 429s to telemetry, apply per-key local throttling + global circuit-breaker.
- Endpoint migration: weighted traffic shift (10/30/60) over a 24–48h window with health probes and automatic rollback.

I've attached a small telemetry schema and a patch with the sample SDK snippets (telemetry_schema_v1.yaml, keystone-sdk-sample.patch). Please confirm if the schema aligns with your observability team conventions or if you'd like us to map to your existing attributes.

Next step: can we lock 60 minutes on Thursday (Aug 26) for an implementation Q/A and a run-through of the sample code?

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: telemetry_schema_v1.yaml (YAML stub describing event types: request.start, request.retry, request.fail, request.success, quota.alert)
Attachment: keystone-sdk-sample.patch (diff with Node + Python examples for retry and rate-limit hooks)

Thanks Ava — this looks promising. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Can you share an explicit example for how the SDK surfaces 429 vs 503? We need to know what to alert on and which errors are transient.
2) For the endpoint migration, can you confirm whether session affinity (cookie/header) will be preserved during weighted shifts?
3) Our compliance folks asked whether audit logs will include the raw request id and model variant served. Is that in the telemetry schema?

Also please include a short snippet for server-side retry logic (we do a small amount of server-side orchestration before relying on SDK recoveries).

—Samir
Director of Integrations, Keystone AI

Samir / team —

Two operational items from our side to call out before the handoff: 

1) KV-cache and prefix caching: if you're doing many short-context calls, enable client-side KV cache to drop p95 latency and token cost. We'll provide a small Redis-backed adapter in the sample patch.

2) Circuit-breaker: we recommend a global CB that opens when error-rate > 5% for 10 minutes OR sustained 429s across 60s window. When open, show an adaptive page to end users and switch to a smaller model variant as fallback. Example header we surface in responses: x-rw-fallback: model-sm-v1; x-rw-request-id: 8f2b...

I'll join the Aug 26 call and bring cutover runbooks and an automatable rollback script (kubectl + traffic router flags) so your SRE can do a dry run.

—Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
